content.thinking:
I'm checking the first claim: the monthly spend totals shown to shoppers who bought something this month were lower than what they actually spent. The cause appears to be that purchases recorded after the change left the stored figure behind, so I'm working out which shoppers that covers, since purchases made before November 4 were counted correctly.

I'm weighing whether to flag that "shoppers who made purchases this month" is slightly broader than the cause: only those with purchases after November 4 are actually affected, not someone whose only purchases came on November 1 through 3. I'm leaning toward treating the statement as supported, since the monthly totals are plausibly what shoppers see.

I'm going through the remaining claims about the duration figure, Argus's cost estimate, the paging, the suspected cause and its recommendation to roll back, and the draft fix PR #554, which hasn't been run. I'm also checking that neither the rollback nor the draft has changed the shop yet, and both points look supported by the source material.

supported.quote: On io-shop, the monthly spend totals shown to shoppers who made purchases this month came out lower than what they had actually bought.
rows: What a reader saw: Shoppers' monthly spend totals fell short of the purchases behind them

supported.quote: A code change to the shop stopped updating each shopper's saved running total for the month whenever a purchase was recorded.
rows: Why, in plain words: A code change to the shop stopped updating

supported.quote: The shop's statements and checks still read that saved total, so it fell further behind with every purchase.
rows: Why, in plain words: A code change to the shop stopped updating

rows: What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): none so far {customer_loss}

rows: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.
